sanskrit_verse:
तृणं वा यदि वा काष्ठं पुष्पं वा यदि वा फलम् ।
अनापृच्छ्य तु गृह्णानो हस्तच्छेदनमर्हति ॥
transliteration:
tṛṇaṃ vā yadi vā kāṣṭhaṃ puṣpaṃ vā yadi vā phalam |
anāpṛcchya tu gṛhṇāno hastacchedanam arhati ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who takes grass, wood, flowers, or fruits without permission incurs the consequence of hand severance.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in consent and ownership
Capacity-based responsibility applies universally regardless of item value
Restoration logic demands proportional realignment with violated integrity
Consciousness alignment requires acknowledgment of ownership boundaries
executable_legal_axioms: IF agent A appropriates object B without explicit or implicit consent from owner C THEN agent A must undergo completion process for boundary violation
IF unauthorized taking occurs THEN system triggers restorative protocol to reaffirm consent structures
IF act of taking bypasses permission framework THEN automatic reintegration sequence activates for responsible party
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating property rights violations, the Supreme Court must recognize that any unauthorized acquisition—irrespective of material worth—constitutes a breach of dharmic ownership structure. The threshold of responsibility lies solely in the absence of permission; intent or valuation are irrelevant. Restoration involves mandatory acknowledgment and reintegration into lawful transactional flow.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa establishes clear causality between unpermitted taking and structural misalignment within dharma. Anupūrvaśaḥ manifests as sequential disruption of consent-based order. Responsibility is proportionally fixed by the violation's nature, not its magnitude. The prescribed consequence serves not punitive function but restores perceptual and operational integrity to the violated domain.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Requiring full restitution and public acknowledgment of ownership transgression
Boundary Recognition Ritual: Structured ceremony wherein violator re-establishes rightful consent channels
Integrity Restoration Sequence: Guided practice ensuring future alignment with permission-based acquisition
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands executed. Ownership derives from conscious consent. Violation disrupts cosmic order. Restoration prevails over punishment. Consciousness alone judges rightly. Dharma is restored.
